messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 429s for inference-api in us-east-1 since 1945622970; error-rate > 10% over 2m, threshold breached. paging eng-oncall.

sara: saw the alert. this started ~2 minutes after the rate-limit change in the canary group (traffic shift).

mike: confirming — dashboards show 429s on the ingress LB, and backend retries spiking. client-side retries are producing a retry storm.

sara: initial hypothesis: new per-user rate limiter config too aggressive for certain high-throughput customers. canary hit larger tenants.

alex: what is the canary rollout percentage?

sara: 20% in us-east canary.

mike: we should either kill the feature flag for rate-limit or roll back the deploy. which is faster?

alex: killing the flag is fastest if the limiter is behind a flag. ffctl status rate_limit_new -> returns `enabled` for env: us-east-canary.

ops-bot: note: runbook link -> https://runbooks.redwood/rollbacks#rate-limiter (read-only).

sara: trying flag kill now: `ffctl set rate_limit_new off --env us-east-canary --actor=sara`

deploy-bot: ACTION: feature flag update queued by sara. Applying change...

deploy-bot: COMPLETE: feature flag `rate_limit_new` set to `off` in us-east-canary (change_id=chg_2026_03_15_41).

mike: metrics: 429 rate dropping in canary slices, but overall us-east still elevated — looks like cross-customer retries are still hitting other nodes.

sara: rolling back the canary deploy as well to be safe. issuing rollback: `deploy rollback inference-api --to-version v2026-03-14-rc3 --scope=us-east-canary`

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK initiated by sara. Rolling back inference-api -> v2026-03-14-rc3. Estimated completion 90s.

incident-bot: Status update: rollback started at 1945623140. Paging suppressed for 10m while we observe.

alex: checking logs: sample 429 trace ->
```
[2026-03-15T21:05:12Z] ingress: client=acme-corp request_id=abc123 status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded limit=100 window=60s
[2026-03-15T21:05:12Z] proxy: retry=1 upstream=frontend-32 status=502
```

mike: that proxy 502s from upstream retries is what caused some customers to see failures, not just 429s. Need to watch SLO alerts.

ops-bot: Quick customer impact note (auto): ~4% of requests in us-east experienced 5xx or 429 between 1945622960-1945623120. Top affected: acme-corp (heavy), beta-startup (moderate).

sara: rollback finished. deploy-bot: `ROLLBACK COMPLETE` at 1945623225.

mike: observing metrics: 429s back to baseline in 60s window. 5xxs decreasing. looks stable.

alex: can we confirm no rollout to other regions? Release pipeline indicates only us-east-canary was touched.

sara: confirmed. we also opened a quick postmortem ticket: https://pm.redwood/INC-5467

jess: i'm taking over the on-call handoff in 20m. any outstanding actions?

sara: leave it in monitoring for the next 30m, keep pagers on for SLO breach. note in handoff: rollback complete, feature flag off for canary, postmortem created, affected customers notified by CSM.

mike: added checklist: 1) validate replayed requests for acme-corp, 2) verify retry/backoff behavior client-side, 3) coordinate with platform to add a circuit-breaker to protect upstream on retries.

jess: ack. will continue monitoring and escalate to infra if error-rate > 2% for 10m.

incident-bot: Handoff: on-call changed to jess at 1945623360. All critical alerts resumed to on-call.

sara: short note for postmortem: misclassification of high-throughput customers in the canary sampling algorithm + aggressive default rate limits. we'll propose feature-flag-first deployments next time.

jess: copying runbook and ticket into the incident log. I'm available for questions during the handoff window.

mike: thanks all. closing thread when oncall confirms stability. :thumbsup:

jess: closing note at 1945623400: system stable for 10m, demoting incident to sev3 and continuing with follow-ups.
